assumptions: The two arms are independent, randomly assigned and observed over the same window.
Each visitor is counted once and a conversion is counted once.

defaults.default_chosen: A two-sided pooled normal approximation to the two-proportion comparison.
defaults.impact: An exact or sequential test gives a different p-value and a different stopping rule.
defaults.question: Test

defaults.default_chosen: The interval for the difference uses unpooled standard errors at the declared alpha.
defaults.impact: A pooled interval is narrower and is not the usual reporting convention.
defaults.question: Interval

minimum_effect.desc: optional relative lift to detect, as a decimal (10% is 0.10)

power.desc: target power for the sample-size calculation, default 0.8

visitors_a.desc: visitors or users assigned to the control arm

visitors_b.desc: visitors or users assigned to the variant arm

ab_test_two_proportion.intended_use: A two-proportion comparison of two observed arms: rates, absolute and relative lift, the pooled z-test, a two-sided p-value, an interval for the difference and, when a minimum effect is declared, the visitors each arm would need.

The normal approximation needs enough conversions in both arms; sparse arms are refused.

assumptions: Pool costs and driver quantities are declared for one period.
Every product's driver quantities are recorded for every activity it consumes.

defaults.default_chosen: Every pool is allocated in full over the driver quantities declared, with no unused-capacity cost.

defaults.default_chosen: Driver totals are the sum of the declared product quantities, not a separate capacity figure.
defaults.impact: Using practical capacity would need a separate driver total.
defaults.question: Driver totals

activities.desc: one record per activity pool: a name and its cost

allocations.desc: one record per activity-product pair: the driver quantity that product consumed

products.desc: one record per product: a name and its units produced

abc_costing.intended_use: Activity-based costing: a rate per activity from its pool and driver total, each product's allocation from the driver quantities it consumes, and the resulting unit cost.
limitations: No idle-capacity adjustment, activity hierarchy or time-driven ABC.
One period and one currency.
The drivers are the declared ones, not chosen or validated.
abc_costing.unsupported_use: Choosing cost drivers; idle or unused capacity cost; activity hierarchies; time-driven ABC; cost of poor quality.

assumptions: Observations are independent within and between groups.
Group distributions are approximately normal (screened by skewness and kurtosis only).
Group variances are approximately equal (screened by Levene's test).

defaults.default_chosen: Blank, null and declared missing codes are excluded within each group and counted.
defaults.impact: Excluded counts are reported.
defaults.question: Missing-value handling

defaults.default_chosen: One-way independent ANOVA (F test), two-sided, comparing group means.
defaults.impact: Repeated-measures, two-way and ANCOVA designs are not supported.
defaults.question: Test

defaults.default_chosen: Eta-squared (between-group SS over total SS), with Cohen-style cut-offs 0.01, 0.06, 0.14 [UNVERIFIED conventions].
defaults.impact: Omega-squared (less biased) is not reported.
defaults.question: Effect size

defaults.default_chosen: If any group's skewness or excess kurtosis exceeds the declared limits, or Levene's test for equal variances rejects at the declared level, switch to Kruskal-Wallis as a logged amendment.
defaults.impact: Kruskal-Wallis compares rank distributions, not means.
defaults.question: Assumption screens and fallback

defaults.default_chosen: The omnibus F test makes no pairwise comparisons, so no correction is applied.

defaults.question: Multiple comparisons

groups.desc: three or more groups: name -> observations (letters and underscores in names; sizes may differ)

anova.intended_use: Compare the means of three or more independent groups with an omnibus F test, an eta-squared effect size and per-group summaries.
limitations: Normality and Levene screen limits are conventional placeholders [UNVERIFIED].
Independence is not tested.
No post-hoc pairwise comparisons or repeated-measures designs.
Eta-squared is a sample effect size and is not bias-corrected.
anova.unsupported_use: Repeated measures; two-way or factorial designs; post-hoc pairwise tests; causal claims; fewer than three groups.

assumptions: The three credit columns describe the same conversions under three rules.
Every conversion is allocated in full under each rule.

defaults.default_chosen: The counts under each rule are declared by you, as reported by your analytics tool or worked out by hand.

defaults.question: Credit counts

defaults.default_chosen: First-click, last-click and linear only.
defaults.impact: Position-based, time-decay and data-driven rules would give different shares.
defaults.question: Rules compared

channels.desc: two to twelve channels, each with its declared credited conversions under the three rules

attribution_split.intended_use: Compare the credit each channel receives under first-click, last-click and linear attribution from the credit counts you declare, and show the largest share disagreement.
limitations: Declared-count arithmetic; no touchpoint log, path or window is processed.
Credit is not causation and no incrementality is measured.
Only three rules are compared.
attribution_split.unsupported_use: Allocating credit from raw touchpoint logs; time-decay or data-driven models; incrementality or holdout estimation; deciding which model is correct.

assumptions: The three account balances use one sign convention and one period.
Errors and omissions are declared or zero.
GDP, if used, is on the same basis.

defaults.default_chosen: All balances use the same declared sign convention and are added; the method checks the identity, not the convention.
defaults.impact: Mixing conventions can make a balanced position look unbalanced.
defaults.question: Sign convention

defaults.default_chosen: A zero net balance is an accounting identity, not a sustainability verdict.
defaults.impact: A balanced position can still hide risky composition.
defaults.question: Interpretation

gdp.desc: optional nominal GDP for the current-account ratio

balance_of_payments.intended_use: Balance-of-payments identity from declared current, capital and financial account balances, with an optional errors term and current-account-to-GDP ratio.
limitations: No reserve valuation, debt-service or sustainability analysis.
No decomposition into trade, income and transfers.
The identity does not validate the underlying data.
balance_of_payments.unsupported_use: Retrieving balance-of-payments data; choosing a sign convention; reserve valuation effects; debt-service or sustainability analysis.

assumptions: The bond is plain-vanilla: fixed coupon, fixed maturity, no embedded options.
One yield to maturity discounts every cash flow.
The price is on a coupon date.

defaults.default_chosen: Declare a yield to get a price, or declare a price to get a yield. Supplying both prices from the yield and reports the declared yield.
defaults.impact: A price and a yield that disagree mean one of them is stale; the method does not choose between them.
defaults.question: Which way is the bond calculated?

defaults.default_chosen: Coupons are paid at the declared frequency and the bond is priced on a coupon date with no accrued interest.
defaults.impact: Between coupon dates the clean price and the cash price differ.
defaults.question: Coupon timing

coupon_rate.desc: ANNUAL coupon rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.08 for 8%

price.desc: market price to solve the yield from; leave blank if you supply the yield

yield_to_maturity.desc: annual yield as a decimal, to price the bond; leave blank if you supply a price instead

bond_analysis.intended_use: Price a plain fixed-coupon bond from its yield, or solve its yield from a declared price, and report Macaulay and modified duration, convexity, DV01 and current yield.
limitations: No accrued interest or day-count convention.
No credit, liquidity or tax adjustment.
Duration and convexity are local parallel-shift sensitivities, not forecasts.
bond_analysis.unsupported_use: Accrued interest between coupon dates; day-count conventions; callable, convertible, floating or amortizing bonds; a spot/forward curve; credit spreads; a traded quote.

assumptions: Linear cost and revenue.
The expected volume is the owner's declared input, not a forecast.

defaults.default_chosen: Fixed cost is constant and unit price and variable cost are constant.
defaults.impact: Break-even moves if costs are stepped or prices change with volume.
defaults.question: Cost behavior

defaults.default_chosen: Both are reported only when expected_units or target_profit is declared; neither is assumed.
defaults.impact: A different expected volume changes the margin of safety but not the break-even point.
defaults.question: Margin of safety and target profit

expected_units.desc: optional expected sales volume, for the margin of safety

target_profit.desc: optional pre-tax profit target, for the required volume

breakeven.intended_use: Units needed to cover fixed cost at a constant unit contribution, with the break-even revenue, contribution margin, margin of safety and target-profit volume when those inputs are declared.
limitations: Single product; a mix needs multi_product_breakeven.
No tax, financing or working-capital effects.
The margin of safety is relative to the declared expected volume only.
breakeven.unsupported_use: Multi-product mix; step-fixed costs; non-linear price or cost; a demand response to the price; tax; financing cost.

assumptions: The aggregates are one period's declared values in one currency.
The debt stock is at the start of the period.
The interest rate is interest paid divided by the debt stock.

defaults.default_chosen: government_spending is primary spending and excludes interest; total spending adds interest.
defaults.impact: Including interest in spending would double-count it in the overall balance.
defaults.question: What spending includes

defaults.default_chosen: The debt-ratio change is (interest rate - nominal growth) x debt ratio - primary balance ratio, with the declared rates held constant.
defaults.impact: A different growth or interest assumption changes the path.
defaults.question: Debt dynamics

debt_stock.desc: the debt stock at the start of the period

inflation_rate.desc: optional inflation rate for the real interest rate

budget_debt.intended_use: Overall and primary budget balances, the debt-to-GDP ratio, the interest rate and the standard debt-ratio change from declared budget aggregates.
limitations: No contingent liabilities, off-budget items or debt composition.
No forecast path or stochastic stress test.
The debt-ratio change is an identity, not a sustainability verdict.
budget_debt.unsupported_use: Forecasting debt; contingent liabilities, off-budget items, currency composition or maturity structure; a full debt-sustainability model; choosing a fiscal rule.

assumptions: One calendar applies to every activity.
Durations count working periods only.
The graph is acyclic.

defaults.default_chosen: A declared list of working period numbers; no weekday or holiday convention is assumed.
defaults.impact: A different calendar changes every date and float.
defaults.question: Calendar

defaults.default_chosen: A zero-duration activity sits on the first working period at or after its constraint.

defaults.question: Zero-duration milestones

activities.desc: one row per activity: id, whole-period duration and optional predecessors

working_periods.desc: comma-separated period numbers that are working, for example 0,1,2,5,6,7

calendar_schedule.intended_use: Schedule declared activities over a declared working calendar: early and late dates, float, the critical path and the calendar duration with non-working gaps.

Float is measured in calendar periods, not working periods.
The calendar must be long enough for the declared durations.
calendar_schedule.unsupported_use: Inferring weekends, holidays or shifts; per-activity calendars; resource limits; dates rather than period numbers; probabilistic durations.

assumptions: Impressions, clicks, conversions and revenue cover the same campaign and period.
A conversion is the action you declared, counted once per acquisition.

defaults.default_chosen: The conversions and revenue are the ones you declare for the period; no window is applied.

defaults.question: Break-even return

clicks.desc: clicks recorded in the same period

contribution_margin_rate.desc: optional contribution margin as a fraction of revenue, for break-even return on ad spend

conversions.desc: conversions you define and count in the same period

revenue.desc: revenue you attribute to the campaign; enter 0 when none is attributable

campaign_efficiency.intended_use: Click-through, cost per click, cost per thousand impressions, conversion rate, cost per acquisition, return on ad spend and advertising cost of sales from the campaign counts you declare, with break-even return on ad spend when a contribution margin is declared.

No incrementality, overlap, view-through or assisted-conversion adjustment.
Revenue and spend must share a currency and a period.
campaign_efficiency.unsupported_use: Reading an ad platform; reconciling platform and analytics numbers; choosing the attribution window; incrementality; cross-campaign overlap; automated bidding or budget recommendations.

assumptions: The pre-money value and the investment are agreed and declared.
All existing shares are counted in founders_shares.
The option pool, if any, is post-money.

defaults.default_chosen: One priced round with ordinary shares; every other instrument and clause is out of scope.

founders_shares.desc: shares outstanding before the round (founders and any existing holders)

investment.desc: the new money invested in this round

option_pool_pct.desc: optional post-money option pool as a fraction of the fully diluted company, default 0

pre_money_valuation.desc: the agreed value of the company before the new money

cap_table_round.intended_use: One priced equity round: post-money value, price per share, new shares, the investor and founder percentages and the dilution, with an optional post-money option pool.

One round only; no note, SAFE or bridge.
The valuation is an input, not a recommendation.

assumptions: Every resource is available for the declared hours and works at the declared minutes per unit.
One product passes through every resource once.

defaults.default_chosen: The resource with the smallest capacity; throughput is that capacity.

defaults.question: Bottleneck

demand.desc: optional demand for the period, for utilisation and the capacity gap

resources.desc: one record per resource: a name, the hours available in the period and the minutes it needs per unit

capacity_analysis.intended_use: Process capacity per resource from available hours and minutes per unit, the bottleneck resource and, when demand is declared, each resource's utilisation and the capacity gap.

Single product and a fixed routing.
Capacity is steady-state, not a queue simulation.
capacity_analysis.unsupported_use: Scheduling, sequencing, batching or buffer design; changeover and maintenance losses; multi-product routings; variability and queueing at each step.

assumptions: The risk-free rate, market return and beta are the owner's declarations or an estimate from the supplied series.

The debt-to-equity ratio is at market values.

defaults.default_chosen: Only applied when debt_to_equity is declared; the tax rate defaults to zero when omitted.

defaults.question: Hamada relevering

beta.desc: beta of the asset or firm; leave blank to estimate it from the two return series

debt_to_equity.desc: debt divided by equity at market values, for Hamada relevering; leave blank if not needed

market_return.desc: expected annual market return as a decimal, e.g. 0.10

returns_asset.desc: the asset's periodic returns, one per period, used only when beta is not declared

returns_market.desc: the market's returns for the same periods, used only when beta is not declared

risk_free_rate.desc: annual risk-free rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.04

tax_rate.desc: corporate tax rate as a decimal, used only with debt_to_equity

capm.intended_use: Compute the CAPM cost of equity from a declared risk-free rate, market return and beta, estimating beta from two return series when it is not declared, and relever or unlever it with Hamada when a debt-to-equity ratio is supplied.

No multi-factor, conditional or downside beta.
The tax rate is a declared input, not computed.
capm.unsupported_use: Choosing the market index, the risk-free proxy or the return interval; multi-factor models; testing whether beta is stable; a market risk premium that is retrieved rather than declared.

assumptions: The net flow is the same every month except for the declared growth.
Month-end receipts and payments; no financing inflow.

defaults.default_chosen: One declared net monthly flow, optionally growing at a constant monthly rate.

defaults.default_chosen: If the declared flow does not burn cash, the method blocks instead of reporting an infinite or capped number.

defaults.question: No finite runway

monthly_net_cash_flow.desc: cash received minus cash paid in a month; must be negative for a runway

opening_cash.desc: cash on hand at the start

target_months.desc: horizon for the lowest balance and funding gap, default 12 (a whole number from 1 to 120)

cash_runway.intended_use: Months of cash left from a declared opening balance and monthly net cash flow, with optional monthly growth, the lowest balance and the funding gap over a declared horizon.

Growth is applied to the net flow, not separately to revenue and costs.
The funding gap ignores the cost of raising the money.
cash_runway.unsupported_use: Forecasting revenue or costs; a cash-flow statement with receipts and payments; seasonality; financing inflows; tax and working-capital timing.

assumptions: Customers are attributed to the channel that won them, with no double counting.
The contribution margin and churn are stable for the period.

defaults.default_chosen: Each channel carries only the spend you assign to it; shared or brand spend is not allocated.

defaults.question: Shared spend

defaults.default_chosen: Lifetime value is the contribution margin divided by the declared churn rate, a period value with no discounting.

defaults.question: Lifetime value

channels.desc: two to twelve channels, each with spend, new customers, contribution margin per customer and period churn

channel_economics.intended_use: Customer acquisition cost, payback, lifetime value and the lifetime-value-to-acquisition-cost ratio for each declared channel, with the blended acquisition cost and each channel's share of spend.

No saturation, seasonality, cross-channel effect or incrementality.
Lifetime value is a single-rate period value, not a survival model.

assumptions: Observations are independent and each is counted in exactly one cell.
Expected counts are large enough (screened; at least 5).

defaults.default_chosen: If any expected count is below 5, the analysis blocks (fail-closed) instead of reporting an unreliable p-value.

defaults.default_chosen: Cramer's V, with coarse cut-offs 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 [UNVERIFIED conventions].
defaults.impact: The interpretation of V depends on the table dimensions.
defaults.question: Effect size

table.desc: a table of non-negative whole-number counts (rows x columns)

Cramer's V cut-offs are coarse [UNVERIFIED].

acquisition_cost.desc: optional cost of winning the customer, for the value ratio and payback

churn_rate.desc: share of customers lost each period, as a decimal (4% is 0.04)

horizon_periods.desc: periods to value, default 12, at most 60

margin_per_period.desc: contribution margin the customer leaves in one period

assumptions: Every cohort is observed for the same number of periods.

assumptions: The cash flows and the discount rate are the owner's declared inputs.

n1.desc: sample size of group 1 (or the single sample for one_sample)

sd1.desc: standard deviation of group 1 (or the single sample)

target_power.desc: power used to compute the minimum detectable effect, default 0.8

power_analysis.intended_use: Plan a two-sample or one-sample comparison of means: the power for a stated effect, and the minimum detectable effect at a declared target power, under the normal approximation.
limitations: Normal approximation; no noncentral t exactness.
No clustering, weights or repeated measures.
Power describes the design, not the study's actual outcome.
power_analysis.unsupported_use: Exact power under the noncentral t distribution; proportions or counts; cluster, weighted or repeated-measures designs; multiplicity; treating a high power as a guarantee of significance.

assumptions: Linear demand and supply, all else equal.
The control is a single fixed price that is enforced.
The market is competitive and partial equilibrium.

defaults.default_chosen: A ceiling binds only below the equilibrium price; a floor binds only above it.
defaults.impact: A non-binding control leaves the market at equilibrium.
defaults.question: Binding test

defaults.default_chosen: The short side of the market determines quantity traded.

defaults.question: Quantity traded

demand_slope.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, must be positive

supply_slope.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, must be positive

price_control.intended_use: The effect of a declared price ceiling or floor on a linear competitive market: quantity traded, shortage or surplus, and deadweight loss.
limitations: No rationing, queues, black markets or quality adjustment.
No dynamics or general-equilibrium effects.
Deadweight loss is the triangle between the declared linear curves.
price_control.unsupported_use: Estimating the curves; rationing, queues or black markets; quality changes; dynamic or general-equilibrium effects; a control that is not a single fixed price.

assumptions: The two markets are separable and resale is impossible.
Demand is linear and marginal cost is constant.
The firm can set a different price in each market.

defaults.default_chosen: Third degree: a separate linear price in each market, with no resale.
defaults.impact: If resale is possible the two prices collapse toward one.
defaults.question: Discrimination

defaults.default_chosen: Constant marginal cost across both markets.
defaults.impact: Different costs or capacity constraints change both prices.
defaults.question: Cost

demand_intercept_1.desc: intercept of demand in market one

demand_intercept_2.desc: intercept of demand in market two

demand_slope_1.desc: positive slope of demand in market one

demand_slope_2.desc: positive slope of demand in market two

price_discrimination.intended_use: Third-degree price discrimination across two separated linear markets with constant marginal cost: quantities, prices and profit.
limitations: No arbitrage, capacity, menu cost or fixed cost.
No welfare comparison with a single price.
Two markets only.
price_discrimination.unsupported_use: Estimating demand; arbitrage or market separation; first- or second-degree discrimination; menu costs, capacity or welfare comparison with a single price.

assumptions: Unit cost and fixed cost are constant over the declared range.
The expected volume is the owner's declared figure.

defaults.default_chosen: The cost-plus price marks up the cost; the margin price divides the cost by one minus the declared margin. Both are shown separately.
defaults.impact: Treating a margin as a markup understates the price.
defaults.question: Markup versus margin

defaults.default_chosen: The declared expected units are used for the break-even and target-return prices.
defaults.impact: A different volume changes both prices.
defaults.question: Volume

expected_units.desc: units expected to be sold in the period

fixed_cost.desc: total fixed cost for the period, default 0

markup_rate.desc: markup on cost as a decimal, e.g. 0.60 for 60%

target_margin_rate.desc: optional margin on the price, greater than zero and below one

target_profit.desc: optional profit target for the period

pricing_decision.intended_use: Cost-plus, target-margin, break-even and target-return prices from declared unit cost, fixed cost, volume and rate inputs.
limitations: No demand response, competitor price or price elasticity.
No discounts, VAT or other taxes.
A target-return price is arithmetic, not a recommendation.
pricing_decision.unsupported_use: Researching willingness to pay or competitor prices; estimating a demand response; psychological pricing; discounts and promotions; tax.

assumptions: The outcome is binary and observations are independent.
The latent index is linear in the predictor.
No separation or near-separation.

defaults.default_chosen: Maximum likelihood by Newton-Raphson on the probit likelihood.
defaults.impact: Logit or a linear probability model gives different coefficients.
defaults.question: Estimator

defaults.default_chosen: Reported at the mean of the predictor; it is not a constant effect.
defaults.impact: A marginal effect at a different x changes the number.
defaults.question: Marginal effect

x.desc: the numeric predictor, same length as y

probit.intended_use: Binary probit with one predictor: latent-index coefficients, log likelihood, McFadden pseudo R-squared and the marginal effect at the mean.
limitations: One predictor only; no controls or interactions.
No robust, clustered or bootstrapped standard errors.
Separation is refused rather than penalised.
probit.unsupported_use: Multiple predictors, interactions, robust or clustered inference, separation, causal claims, or predicted probabilities outside the observed support.

assumptions: Observations are in time order and come from one process.
The process is approximately stable apart from the signals reported.

defaults.default_chosen: Individuals with moving ranges, limits at the mean plus or minus three estimated sigmas (MRbar / 1.128).
defaults.impact: A subgroup chart needs subgroup sizes and different constants.
defaults.question: Chart type

defaults.default_chosen: A point outside the limits, or a run of eight on one side of the mean.
defaults.impact: More Western Electric rules would flag more patterns.
defaults.question: Signals

spec_upper.desc: optional upper specification limit, declared with the lower one

process_control.intended_use: An individuals chart with moving ranges: mean, estimated sigma, three-sigma control limits, out-of-control points, the longest run on one side of the mean and, when specification limits are declared, Cp and Cpk.
limitations: I-MR only; no subgroup charts, EWMA, CUSUM or multivariate charts.
Capability uses the within-series sigma and the declared specification; no threshold is applied.
The chart is descriptive; it does not prove future stability.
process_control.unsupported_use: Subgroup charts (X-bar/R, p, c, u), EWMA or CUSUM; capability indices from a stable-process study; measurement-system analysis; automatic alarm logic beyond the declared rules.

assumptions: The firm faces the declared linear demand curve.
The cost function is quadratic and non-decreasing.
The firm is a single-price monopolist or monopoly-like seller.

defaults.default_chosen: A single-price firm facing the declared downward-sloping demand curve; MR = MC.
defaults.impact: A price-taking firm sets price equal to marginal cost instead.
defaults.question: Market structure

defaults.default_chosen: TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with non-negative coefficients.
defaults.impact: A different cost function changes the optimum.
defaults.question: Cost function

demand_slope.desc: b in P = a - bQ, must be positive

profit_maximization.intended_use: Profit-maximising quantity and price for a firm facing linear demand P = a - bQ and quadratic cost TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with revenue, cost, profit, markup and the Lerner index.
limitations: Single product and single period.
No price discrimination, strategic interaction or entry.
The result is arithmetic on the declared curves, not evidence about a real market.
profit_maximization.unsupported_use: Estimating demand or cost; multi-product firms; price discrimination; entry, dynamics or strategic interaction; a competitive market price taken as given.

assumptions: Revenue, margin, costs and depreciation are declared for each period; interest and principal follow declared lists or the declared opening loan terms.
Working capital follows the declared days on revenue and cost of sales.
Tax applies to positive pre-tax profit at the declared rate.

defaults.default_chosen: Annual periods in one currency; revenue and cost lists must be the same length.
defaults.impact: Monthly periods need their own declared list and days basis.
defaults.question: Period and currency

defaults.default_chosen: Cash, receivables, inventory, net fixed assets, payables, loan and equity; the opening balance must balance and every period is checked.
defaults.impact: An unbalanced opening balance is refused with the equity that would balance it.
defaults.question: Balance sheet

capex.desc: optional capital expenditure each period, default zero

gross_margin_rate.desc: gross margin as a fraction of revenue, e.g. 0.40

interest.desc: interest expense each period; omit when loan terms are declared

inventory_days.desc: inventory days of cost of sales, default 0

loan_annual_rate.desc: optional annual interest rate on the opening loan, e.g. 0.09

loan_principal.desc: optional opening loan principal; with the rate and years, the interest and principal are derived

loan_years.desc: optional number of level annual payments; must equal the number of periods

opening_equity.desc: opening equity; the opening balance sheet must balance

operating_costs.desc: fixed operating costs each period, excluding depreciation and interest

payable_days.desc: payable days of cost of sales, default 0

principal_repayment.desc: loan principal repaid each period; omit when loan terms are declared

revenue.desc: declared revenue for each period, one to ten periods

tax_rate.desc: tax rate on positive pre-tax profit, default 0

proforma_statements.intended_use: Projected income statement, cash flow and balance sheet from declared revenue, margin, costs, depreciation, interest and principal (or a declared opening loan), tax and working-capital days, with the balance check.
limitations: No forecast, tax payable, dividends, new borrowing beyond the opening loan, deferred tax or disposals.
One product and one currency; annual periods only.
The balance check is an identity only when the declared inputs are internally consistent.
proforma_statements.unsupported_use: Forecasting demand; deriving revenue; tax rules; dividends; new borrowing; deferred tax; asset disposals; monthly periods; multi-product statements.

assumptions: Crash cost is linear between normal and crash durations.
Durations are whole periods and the graph is acyclic.
Crashing one critical activity does not change scope or quality.

defaults.default_chosen: Linear between the normal and crash durations; the declared crash_cost is the total premium to reach the crash duration.
defaults.impact: A non-linear or shared cost changes the plan.
defaults.question: Crash cost

defaults.default_chosen: Greedy: one period at a time on the cheapest available critical activity, recomputing the network each step.
defaults.impact: This is not a linear-programming optimum.
defaults.question: Search rule

activities.desc: one row per activity: id, normal_duration, crash_duration, crash_cost and optional predecessors

project_crashing.intended_use: Crash a declared schedule to a target duration: the activity periods bought, the resulting duration and the total crash cost.
limitations: Greedy, not globally optimal.
No calendars, resource limits, non-linear costs or quality trade-off.
A target below the fully crashed duration is refused.
project_crashing.unsupported_use: Finding the least-cost crash plan globally; non-linear, shared or step crash costs; crashing with resource limits, calendars or uncertain durations.

assumptions: The cash flows are after tax and after any financing the owner intends to include.
The discount rate is the right hurdle for this project's risk.
The first flow is the outlay.

defaults.default_chosen: MIRR reinvests positive flows at the declared finance rate (default: the discount rate) and finances negative flows at the discount rate.
defaults.impact: A different reinvestment rate changes MIRR but not NPV.
defaults.question: Reinvestment convention

defaults.default_chosen: End-of-period flows with the first at t=0, matching the npv and irr methods.
defaults.impact: Mid-year flows would raise the present value.
defaults.question: Timing

cashflows.desc: cash flows, first at t=0 (normally the negative outlay), then one per period

finance_rate.desc: rate at which positive flows are reinvested for MIRR; default is the discount rate

rate.desc: discount rate (cost of capital) per period, e.g. 0.10

project_metrics.intended_use: Report the profitability index, modified internal rate of return, simple payback and equivalent annual annuity of one declared project alongside its NPV and IRR, so the ranking measures can be compared.
limitations: No tax, depreciation shield or working-capital release.
Payback ignores everything after recovery; EAA assumes a repeatable project.
The IRR is reported only when a single root exists.
project_metrics.unsupported_use: Choosing the cash flows, the discount rate or the reinvestment rate; unequal-risk projects; capital rationing; real options; tax and depreciation shields; mid-year timing.

assumptions: Outcomes are evaluated relative to the declared reference point.
Probabilities are known and sum to one.
The parameters are the owner's declared values.

defaults.default_chosen: Gains are curved with the gain parameter; losses with the loss parameter and multiplied by loss aversion.
defaults.impact: Different parameters change the prospect value and the ranking of gambles.
defaults.question: Value function

defaults.default_chosen: Tversky-Kahneman-style weights, normalised to sum to one.

defaults.question: Probability weights

outcomes.desc: outcomes to be evaluated relative to the reference

probabilities.desc: probabilities, same length, summing to one

prospect_theory.intended_use: Kahneman-Tversky-style prospect value from declared outcomes, probabilities and a reference point, with loss aversion, curvature and probability weighting.
limitations: A declared parameterisation, not an estimate.
No cumulative rank-dependent weighting, ambiguity or framing.
Descriptive, not normative.
prospect_theory.unsupported_use: Estimating the parameters; a normative recommendation; ambiguity, framing or reference-point selection; cumulative prospect theory with rank dependence.

assumptions: Two individuals with declared linear marginal benefits.
The good is non-rival and non-excludable.
Marginal cost is linear and positive.

defaults.default_chosen: Vertical summation of the two marginal-benefit schedules (the Samuelson condition).
defaults.impact: Horizontal summation would be the private-good case, not the public-good case.
defaults.question: Aggregation

defaults.default_chosen: The efficient quantity is where summed marginal benefit equals marginal cost.
defaults.impact: A voluntary-contribution equilibrium would generally underprovide.
defaults.question: Provision

mb1_intercept.desc: intercept of the first marginal-benefit schedule

mb1_slope.desc: positive slope of the first marginal-benefit schedule

mb2_intercept.desc: intercept of the second marginal-benefit schedule

mb2_slope.desc: positive slope of the second marginal-benefit schedule

public_good.intended_use: Efficient provision of a public good from two declared linear marginal-benefit schedules and one marginal-cost schedule, with total and net benefit.
limitations: Two individuals only; no free-riding or contribution game.
No distributional weights, crowding out or administrative cost.
The benefit schedules are declared, not estimated.
public_good.unsupported_use: Estimating benefits; free-riding games; contribution mechanisms; crowding out; distributional weights; more than two individuals.

assumptions: The intent counts are from one declared sample.
The weights are the owner's declared convention.
The population is the market the sample is meant to represent.

defaults.default_chosen: Definitely 0.8, probably 0.3, maybe 0.1 and never 0; every weight is declared and shown.
defaults.impact: A different weight set changes the intent rate and the projection.

defaults.question: Representativeness

definitely.desc: respondents who said they would definitely buy

never.desc: respondents who said they would not buy

price.desc: optional price to convert projected buyers into revenue

probably.desc: respondents who said they would probably buy

target_population.desc: optional population to project buyers onto

purchase_intent.intended_use: A weighted purchase-intent rate from declared survey counts, with a projected buyer count and revenue when a population and a price are declared.
limitations: Stated intent overstates purchase; no calibration against actual sales.
No sampling error, non-response, seasonality or price response.
The weights are conventions, not estimates.
purchase_intent.unsupported_use: Choosing the conversion weights for you; sampling, non-response or representativeness; turning stated intent into a forecast; statistical inference.

assumptions: Arrivals are random and independent at a constant average rate.
Service times are exponential with a constant average rate per server.
Servers are interchangeable, with one queue and no priority or abandonment.

defaults.default_chosen: First come, first served, identical servers, unlimited queue capacity.
defaults.impact: Priorities or a finite waiting room give different waits.
defaults.question: Queue discipline

defaults.default_chosen: Random arrivals and service times with exponential inter-arrival and service distributions.

defaults.question: Variability

servers.desc: number of interchangeable servers, default 1 (a whole number from 1 to 50)

service_rate.desc: average customers served per period by one server

queue_analysis.intended_use: A multi-server M/M/c queue: utilisation, average customers in the queue and in the system, the average waits, the probability the system is empty and the probability a customer waits.
limitations: No priorities, abandonment, batch arrivals or heterogeneous servers.
The exponential assumption can understate or overstate real queues.
At or above servers x service rate the queue never clears and the method blocks.
queue_analysis.unsupported_use: Priorities; balking, reneging or batch arrivals; non-exponential service or arrival patterns; heterogeneous servers; scheduling or simulation.

assumptions: The figures are as reported for one period, in one currency and on one accounting basis.
Balance-sheet figures are period-end balances.

defaults.default_chosen: None are applied, because none is supplied or verified. Ratios are computed, not rated.
defaults.impact: Whether a value is good or bad is left to the reader and the context.

defaults.default_chosen: Period-end balances and a 365-day year for the efficiency ratios.

cost_of_sales.desc: cost of sales for the period

current_assets.desc: current assets at the period end

current_liabilities.desc: current liabilities at the period end

interest_expense.desc: interest expense for the period, as a positive amount

net_income.desc: net income for the period (as supplied; no tax computation is performed)

The figures are not validated against a trial balance here; use the management-accounts method for a bookkeeping-level check.
There is no tax computation; net income is used exactly as supplied.
ratio_analysis.unsupported_use: Benchmarks, industry averages or pass/fail judgements; GAAP or IFRS presentation; restating or adjusting figures; multi-period comparatives; segment, consolidated or multi-currency analysis; forecasting.

assumptions: The project value follows a binomial lattice with constant volatility and rate.
The option is on the declared project value, not a traded asset.
Exercise is European or American as declared.

defaults.question: Real-option caveat

horizon_years.desc: time to expiry in years, default one

investment_cost.desc: the strike or investment needed to exercise

option_type.desc: call (option to invest) or put (option to abandon)

risk_free_rate.desc: annual risk-free rate as a decimal

underlying_value.desc: the project or asset value today

No continuous hedging or market-price comparison.
One option at a time; no compound or interacting options.

assumptions: Treatment is determined by the running variable crossing the cutoff.

data.desc: one record per observation: the running variable and the outcome

No robust or clustered inference.

assumptions: Items are continuous or roughly interval and measure one construct.

assumptions: Each activity consumes one declared resource at a constant demand for its whole duration.

assumptions: The net gain and investment are the owner's declared figures.
